questions.question: Tailgating (driving too close to another car's rear bumper):

options.text: Cannot result in a traffic ticket.
Prevents other cars from cutting you off.

questions.explanation: Tailgating frustrates drivers and can lead to aggressive driving. You can get a ticket for unsafe driving.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot every time you move your car. This includes turning, changing lanes, and pulling toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: Driving too fast:

options.text: Saves time and gets you to your destination faster.
Increases the risk of serious injury and death.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases the risk of serious injury and death.
questions.explanation: Excessive speed is a major cause of car crashes. It does not save time and leads to dangerous decisions.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol.
questions.explanation: Only time lowers your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may keep you awake, but they do not change your BAC.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive only in the direction shown by the arrow.
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign that tells drivers what they must do. You must drive in the direction of the arrow.

questions.question: Before driving after snow, clear snow and ice from your car's:
questions.explanation: Clear all windows so you can see. Keep your headlights, brake lights, and taillights clean so other drivers can see you.

questions.question: When you approach railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate closes.
Not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look both ways, listen for trains, slow down, and be prepared to stop for any trains or vehicles.

questions.question: At a railroad crossing with no train in sight, you must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if lights are flashing, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is present, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is close. Never race a train.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that people cross here. Watch for pedestrians entering the crosswalk. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to places where animals, people, and bicycles may cross the road.

questions.question: If you have had several beers, alcohol's effects will only be reduced by:
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. Cold showers, coffee, or exercise will not speed this up. It takes about one hour for your body to process one drink.

questions.question: Before returning to your original lane after passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: When passing, check your rearview mirror. You should see both headlights of the vehicle you passed before you return to your original lane.

questions.question: What is the only proven way to remove alcohol or drugs from your system?
questions.explanation: Cold showers, coffee, and exercise do not lower your blood alcohol level. Only time will reduce alcohol and drugs in your system.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.
You may not see the other vehicle's brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: Following too closely means you cannot stop in time if the car ahead brakes suddenly. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: Night driving is more difficult than day driving because:

options.text: Cars overheat more quickly at night.
Visibility is reduced in the dark.
It is more likely to be raining at night.
You are more likely to encounter a motorcycle at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Visibility is reduced in the dark.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead. Use your headlights and drive slowly enough to stop within the distance you can see.

questions.question: The most effective safety restraints in a crash are:

options.text: Only a lap and shoulder belt.
Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.
questions.explanation: Safety belts greatly improve your chances of surviving a crash. Airbags work best when used with safety belts. Always wear both your shoulder and lap belts.

questions.question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol and/or drugs?
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.
Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle, if you can.
questions.explanation: Turn on your emergency flashers to warn other drivers. Stay inside your vehicle if possible. Standing or walking on an interstate is very dangerous because of the high speed traffic.

questions.question: Alcohol:
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your brain activity and reduces skills needed for safe driving. It slows your reaction time and harms your judgment.

questions.question: Drivers should give extra space to children on bicycles because:

options.text: They do not have the same physical reflexes as adults.
They are smaller and more difficult to see than adults.

questions.explanation: Children are unpredictable and hard to see. Be extra careful around schools, bus stops, playgrounds, and parks. Watch for children on bikes near the road, as they may ride into traffic suddenly.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what should you do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.
questions.explanation: Watch for signs of tiredness while driving. You are too tired to drive safely if your eyes are hard to keep open, you drift out of your lane, or you turn up the radio and open windows to stay awake. If you notice these signs, park in a safe place and take a short nap.

questions.question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?

options.text: When a flagger tells you to stop.
When there is a stop sign.
When flashing red lights and gates are working.

questions.explanation: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign tells you to. Also stop when you see flashing red lights and gates that are operating.

questions.question: What should you do to make sure your health does not cause unsafe driving?

options.text: Stay in good physical shape and get regular check-ups.
Know how medicines affect your driving.
Only drive within your physical abilities.

questions.explanation: Your physical health affects how safely you can drive. Know your physical limits and only drive when it is safe for you to do so.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you?

options.text: It makes you feel overly confident.

questions.explanation: Alcohol harms the parts of your brain that control good judgment and self-control. You may feel overly confident or silly after drinking. Alcohol also slows your reaction time, hurts your balance, and makes it hard to judge distance and see clearly. This makes it difficult to react to what is happening around you.

questions.question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees you before you proceed.
Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.
questions.explanation: You must always let pedestrians cross, even if there is no marked crosswalk.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass.
Speed up while they are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Avoid looking at them. Speeding up or blocking them may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: At a crosswalk, who has the right of way?

options.text: Construction workers must yield to you.

questions.explanation: Pedestrians have the right of way at street crossings when they follow traffic signals. At marked or unmarked crosswalks without traffic signals, vehicles must stop for pedestrians.

questions.question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs?

options.text: To make drivers angry about slow traffic.
To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.

questions.correctAnswerText: To keep traffic away from dangerous work areas.
questions.explanation: Work zones are dangerous for both workers and drivers. Watch for cones, barrels, signs, large vehicles, and workers in bright vests as you approach a work zone. These warn you and show you where to go.

questions.question: If you feel tired while driving, what is the best thing to do?
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is as dangerous as driving under the influence of alcohol. If you feel tired while driving, stop driving.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A downgrade or hill is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: A downgrade or hill is coming.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you about a dangerous downgrade or hill ahead. The hill may be very long, steep, or have sharp curves.

questions.question: When should you yield to a pedestrian?

options.text: Only if they are in a crosswalk.
At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
Only if the traffic light favors the pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: At all times, even if they are breaking traffic laws.
questions.explanation: Always watch for pedestrians near your vehicle. You must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, no matter what the circumstances are.

questions.question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, what must you do?

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Pull to the side of the road and stop.
Speed up and take the nearest exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear an emergency vehicle siren, pull to the side of the road or curb and stop.

questions.question: What type of sign is this?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped, yellow, with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or special situations ahead.

questions.question: You see pedestrians near the road. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to leave the area quickly.

questions.explanation: Watch for pedestrians who might cross your path. If you see pedestrians near the road, slow down and be ready to stop if needed.

questions.question: What color are temporary signs in construction and work areas?
questions.explanation: All temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black writing and symbols.

questions.question: What problems can worn or bald tires cause?
questions.explanation: Worn or bald tires increase stopping distance and make turning harder. Tires without enough tread also increase the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You have a green light at an intersection, but pedestrians are crossing against the red light. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up and pass in front of them.
Stop and let them cross safely.
Drive close to them to scare them into following the rules.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let them cross safely.
questions.explanation: Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles that may be in the intersection when you have a green light. Always be careful around pedestrians.

questions.question: What do your brake lights tell other drivers?

options.text: You are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Your brake lights must work properly whenever you drive.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If possible, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency help to arrive.

questions.question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is crossing the street. What should you do?

options.text: Stop until they are completely away from your path.
Honk your horn as you drive past them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop until they are completely away from your path.
questions.explanation: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing the street, you must stop until they are completely away from your path. Always give the right-of-way to blind pedestrians.

questions.question: Where should children age 12 and under sit in a vehicle with airbags?

options.text: The bed of a pick-up truck.

questions.explanation: Airbags can hurt children. Children age 12 and under should always sit in the back seat of a vehicle with airbags.

questions.question: What does this orange triangle symbol mean?
questions.explanation: An orange triangle on the back of a vehicle means it is a slow-moving vehicle. You may see this on farm equipment, roadwork vehicles, or horse-drawn wagons.

questions.question: What is the safe way to cross railroad tracks?

options.text: Look both ways only when the red light is flashing.
Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
Cross very quickly when a train is approaching.
Quickly pass under any lowering gates.

questions.correctAnswerText: Listen, look both ways, and cross only if it is safe.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are dangerous. Always listen and look both ways for trains from either direction. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?

options.text: Pull next to the driver and yell at them.
Flash your high beams at the driver.
Cut them off to get back at them.

questions.explanation: Do not get angry at other drivers. To stay safe, ignore the mistake and keep driving safely.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You do not need to signal your turn.
Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prepare to stop and let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the green turn arrow is ending. You must prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: How can you identify an aggressive driver?

options.text: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
The number of passengers in their car.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make sudden and improper lane changes.
questions.explanation: Watch for drivers making sudden or improper lane changes. If you see an aggressive driver, stay away from them. Do not challenge them.

questions.question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt, what should you do?

options.text: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the lap and shoulder belts.
questions.explanation: Always wear both parts of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part does not protect you well. If you have an automatic shoulder belt, also buckle your lap belt.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: Whenever you need to use them.
Before you get into the car.

questions.explanation: Adjust your mirrors before you drive. Also adjust your seat, fasten your safety belt, and secure all items. Do not adjust mirrors while driving.

questions.question: Which substances can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Cough syrups and cold tablets with codeine or antihistamines.

questions.explanation: Many drugs can impair driving. These include prescription drugs like tranquilizers and sedatives, over-the-counter cough and cold medicines, allergy medicines, and illegal drugs.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing after the "Don't Walk" signal flashes. They are in the middle of the street when your light turns green. What should you do?

options.text: Proceed because you have the right-of-way.
Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.
Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the pedestrian crosses before proceeding.
questions.explanation: At a green light, give the right-of-way to any pedestrians in the intersection. Wait until they have completely crossed before you proceed.
